title: Vesper and the Typewriter
premise: In the winter of 1919, in a river town scarred by war, Wren Dunmore tends the wounded at a convalescent house while secretly recording, in a battered typewriter's carbon copies, the names of soldiers and civilians erased from official reports. When the seasonal bridge closes, Wren is trapped with Major Aldous Vane — the officer whose omissions killed dozens — and must smuggle the ledger past three checkpoints before spring floods destroy the evidence and Vane consolidates his cover-up. Betrayed by an ally, hunted through the frozen town, Wren finds unexpected protectors among the very people they once kept at arm's length: a disgraced telegraph operator, a widow who runs the ferry, and the orphans of the omitted. In the end, Wren chooses exposure over safety, broadcasting the names over the telegraph lines as the bridge reopens — surviving not by silence, but by being finally, irreversibly seen.
about_author: Ada Joubert is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing military correspondence from the Great War and became haunted by the gaps between official record and lived truth. She writes historical fiction about the people history forgot to count.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Names
chapters.summary: Wren Dunmore's POV. Establishes the convalescent house, Wren's nightly ritual of typing the omitted names onto carbon paper hidden inside bandage invoices. Emotional beat: weary vigilance — the quiet cost of ten years of careful silence.

chapters.title: What the Major Doesn't Write
chapters.summary: Wren observes Major Vane dictating a report that erases a failed supply convoy and the eleven men lost with it. Wren types the true version after he leaves. Beat: cold recognition that the enemy of this story wears a friendly face.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Town criers announce the seasonal closure; the last crossing leaves without Wren, who stayed to tend a dying patient. Trapped for months with Vane quartered nearby. Beat: dread blooming into resolve — invisibility has expired.

chapters.title: Carbon Ghosts
chapters.summary: Wren hides the full ledger inside the typewriter's case lining, meeting Odile, the ferry widow, who suspects more than she says. Beat: first fragile alliance; Wren learns trust is a risk worth pricing.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Wren maps the route out: the mill gate, the garrison desk, the river pier — each guarded by men with different loyalties. Beat: strategic hope shadowed by the realization that one of the guards owes Vane everything.

chapters.title: The Telegraph Boy
chapters.summary: Introduces Samir, a teenage telegraph operator struck off the rolls for relaying a dead soldier's last message home. He recognizes what Wren is carrying. Beat: kinship between keepers of erased names; found family begins.

chapters.title: An Inventory of the Missing
chapters.summary: Wren reads the ledger aloud to Samir and Odile in the boathouse — forty-one names. Each listener claims a connection to one. Beat: grief transmuted into purpose; the ledger becomes theirs, not just Wren's.

chapters.title: Vane's Kindness
chapters.summary: Vane, charming and perceptive, gifts Wren new medical supplies and probes gently about 'rumors of a list.' Wren performs gratitude while terror hums beneath. Beat: the corruption of power shown as courtesy; danger dressed as generosity.

chapters.title: The Mill Gate
chapters.summary: First smuggling attempt: Wren passes a single carbon page sewn into a corpse-shipment manifest. It works — barely. Beat: exhilaration curdling into fear when the guard lingers too long on Wren's face.

chapters.title: Orphans of the Omitted
chapters.summary: A girl named Petra, daughter of an erased soldier, catches Wren typing at night and asks if her father's name is in the machine. Beat: devastating tenderness; Wren realizes the ledger was never just evidence — it's inheritance.

chapters.title: A Debt at the Garrison Desk
chapters.summary: Sergeant Halloway, checkpoint two, recognizes Wren from field hospitals and offers passage — but wants the ledger's protection for himself, having signed some of the false reports. Beat: moral compromise; survival demands dirty hands.

chapters.title: Frost on the Wire
chapters.summary: Samir intercepts a coded telegram: Vane has requested authority to 'audit hospital records' before the thaw. Time collapses. Beat: ticking clock made explicit; panic sharpening into speed.

chapters.title: The Boathouse Burns
chapters.summary: A fire destroys the boathouse and half the hidden carbons. Arson is suspected; Odile's son is arrested as a scapegoat. Beat: catastrophic loss and rage; the found family fractures under pressure.

chapters.title: What Petra Saw
chapters.summary: Petra reveals she saw Vane's aide near the boathouse that night. Her testimony is worthless to adults but priceless to Wren. Beat: the powerless holding real power; Wren's protective instinct hardens into strategy.

chapters.title: Halloway's Price
chapters.summary: Halloway demands the original ledger as insurance, revealing he tipped Vane about the audit leak. Wren must decide whether to sacrifice him or the plan. Beat: betrayal within the alliance; trust becomes currency spent carefully.

chapters.title: The Typewriter Confiscated
chapters.summary: Vane's audit seizes the convalescent house records — including the typewriter itself, unaware of its hollow lining. Wren must retrieve it from the garrison strongroom. Beat: audacious heist energy; fear converted to nerve.

chapters.title: Night of the Audit
chapters.summary: Odile creates a diversion at the pier; Samir cuts the telegraph line; Wren slips into the strongroom and empties the typewriter's lining as Vane works ten feet away. Beat: white-knuckle climax of stealth; Wren nearly speaks the truth aloud.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Three
chapters.summary: At the river pier, the final guard — a man whose brother's name is in the ledger — reads one carbon page and steps aside, weeping. Beat: catharsis; the evidence finds its truest escort in grief.

chapters.title: The Thaw
chapters.summary: Vane discovers the theft and orders the bridge held shut, but floodwaters rise faster than his orders travel. The town turns against him as Odile's son is freed. Beat: power's machinery jamming against ordinary solidarity.

chapters.title: Every Name, Out Loud
chapters.summary: Climax: with the wire repaired, Samir broadcasts all forty-one names across every telegraph line in the province while Wren stands at the reopened bridge reading them aloud to the crowd. Beat: triumph and terror fused; silence ends forever.

chapters.title: After the Flood
chapters.summary: Vane is recalled under inquiry; justice is partial, imperfect, but begun. Wren buries the empty typewriter casing by the river and keeps only the names. Beat: bittersweet reckoning; survival's price paid, and worth it.

chapters.title: Vesper
chapters.summary: Epilogue, spring. Wren stays — no longer invisible — teaching Petra to type the town's own stories, the evening bell ringing like a promise. Beat: peace earned; found family settled around a shared act of remembering.
